newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco shares rise after unit sale unveiled.
newsitem.headline: Inco shares rise after unit sale unveiled.

text.p: Inco Ltd shares rose 0.50 to 45.50 in Toronto on Wednesday after the nickel mining giant said it agreed to sell its Inco Alloys International unit for US$410 million.
"They are up on that," one equities trader said.
Inco said earlier today that it agreed to sell its Alloys unit to a division of Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund LP, called Haynes International Inc.
Inco said it expected an after-tax gain of about US$85 million on the sale, which should close in the autumn of 1997.

Inco is still in talks to end a labor dispute after the nickel miner's 4,670 unionized Sudbury, Ontario workers went on strike at midnight on June 2, after voting 60.4 percent against a contract offer endorsed by union leaders.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt.
